2023 saw the ratification of a new [collective bargaining agreement](/wiki/NBA_collective_bargaining_agreement "NBA collective bargaining agreement"), which will penalize teams who exceed the luxury tax above certain "apron" thresholds, making it significantly more difficult for teams to sign multiple superstars to maximum contracts.[[123]](#cite_note-123) Seven different champions were crowned in seven years from 2019 to 2025, the longest such stretch in league history, leading numerous outlets to dub this the "[parity](/wiki/Parity_(sports) "Parity (sports)") era" in contrast to the dynasties which dominated previous decades.[[124]](#cite_note-124)[[125]](#cite_note-125)

> We set out to create a system that allowed for more competition around the league. The goal being to have 30 teams all in the position, if well managed, to compete for championships. And that's what we're seeing here.

— NBA Commissioner [Adam Silver](/wiki/Adam_Silver "Adam Silver") on the NBA's new era of parity[[126]](#cite_note-126)

The [2022–23 season](/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NBA_season "2022–23 NBA season") saw the [Denver Nuggets](/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets"), led by center [Nikola Jokić](/wiki/Nikola_Joki%C4%87 "Nikola Jokić"), make the [franchise's first NBA Finals appearance](/wiki/2023_NBA_Finals "2023 NBA Finals") and defeat the Miami Heat in five games to win their first NBA championship.[[127]](#cite_note-127)

The [2023–24 NBA season](/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_NBA_season "2023–24 NBA season") saw the star-studded Boston Celtics, winning a championship over the Dallas Mavericks, after five [conference finals appearances](/wiki/NBA_conference_finals "NBA conference finals"), and a finals appearance marking their 18th championship, their first since 2008.[[128]](#cite_note-128)

fanoutqa_002058.x:
Colorectal cancer :: Cause :: Diet :: chunk_0002
Diet is the largest environmental risk factor.[[17]](#cite_note-Cause11-17) Alcohol use is the most evidence-supported dietary risk factor.[[4]](#cite_note-Theodoratou2017-4)[[21]](#cite_note-:1-21) Alcohol use above one drink per day increases risk.[[22]](#cite_note-Fedirko2011-22)

[Whole grain](/wiki/Whole_grain "Whole grain") intake is inversely related to risk.[[4]](#cite_note-Theodoratou2017-4) Drinking five glasses of water a day may be linked to a decrease in the risk of colorectal cancer and [adenomatous](/wiki/Adenomatous "Adenomatous") polyps.[[23]](#cite_note-23) The consumption of calcium (e.g. [dairy products](/wiki/Dairy_product "Dairy product")) is protective against colorectal cancer.[[21]](#cite_note-:1-21)

Associated with a diet high in [saturated fats](/wiki/Saturated_fat "Saturated fat"), elevated levels of [bile acids](/wiki/Bile_acid "Bile acid") appear to increase the risk of colorectal cancer.[[24]](#cite_note-Fogelson2023-24)[[25]](#cite_note-Bernstein2023-25) The bile acid [deoxycholic acid](/wiki/Deoxycholic_acid "Deoxycholic acid") particularly is elevated in the colonic contents of humans in response to a high fat diet.[[24]](#cite_note-Fogelson2023-24)[[25]](#cite_note-Bernstein2023-25) In populations that have a high incidence of colorectal cancer, fecal concentrations of bile acids, particularly deoxycholic acid, are higher.[[24]](#cite_note-Fogelson2023-24)[[25]](#cite_note-Bernstein2023-25)

Higher fecal concentrations of the bile acids [cholic acid](/wiki/Cholic_acid "Cholic acid") and [chenodeoxycholic acid](/wiki/Chenodeoxycholic_acid "Chenodeoxycholic acid") are associated with a high risk and higher incidence of colorectal cancer.[[26]](#cite_note-26)

It has a population of 29,558,908 in the urban area as of 2025. The city is located on the [Chinese](/wiki/East_China "East China") shoreline on the southern [estuary](/wiki/Estuary "Estuary") of the [Yangtze River](/wiki/Yangtze_River "Yangtze River"), with the [Huangpu River](/wiki/Huangpu_River "Huangpu River") bisecting the city. Shanghai is a global center for finance, business and economics, research, science and technology, manufacturing, transportation, [tourism](/wiki/List_of_tourist_attractions_in_Shanghai "List of tourist attractions in Shanghai"), and [culture](/wiki/Culture_of_Shanghai "Culture of Shanghai"). The [Port of Shanghai](/wiki/Port_of_Shanghai "Port of Shanghai") is the [world's busiest container port](/wiki/World%27s_busiest_container_port "World's busiest container port").[[13]](#cite_note-13) As of 2022, the Greater Shanghai metropolitan area was estimated to produce a [gross metropolitan product](/wiki/Gross_metropolitan_product "Gross metropolitan product") ([nominal](/wiki/GDP_(nominal) "GDP (nominal)")) of nearly 13 trillion [RMB](/wiki/Renminbi "Renminbi") ($1.9 trillion).[[14]](#cite_note-GDP2022-14)

Fitzpatrick signed a one-year contract with the [Washington Football Team](/wiki/Washington_Football_Team "Washington Football Team") on March 18, 2021.[[165]](#cite_note-165)

Fitzpatrick started in the season-opening 20–16 loss to the [Los Angeles Chargers](/wiki/2021_Los_Angeles_Chargers_season "2021 Los Angeles Chargers season"), but suffered a hip [subluxation](/wiki/Subluxation "Subluxation") during the second quarter, which resulted in his being placed on [injured reserve](/wiki/Injured_reserve "Injured reserve") and missing the rest of the season.[[166]](#cite_note-166)[[167]](#cite_note-167) Due to his brief tenure, Fitzpatrick did not have any touchdowns or interceptions with Washington, the only time he did not do so with a team he played for.[[168]](#cite_note-168)

On June 2, 2022, Fitzpatrick announced his retirement from the NFL after 17 seasons.[[169]](#cite_note-169)[[170]](#cite_note-170)

fanoutqa_017930.t: Alain Prost :: Career legacy :: Appraisals by contemporaries :: chunk_0019
fanoutqa_017930.x:
Alain Prost :: Career legacy :: Appraisals by contemporaries :: chunk_0019
In 2009, an *[Autosport](/wiki/Autosport "Autosport")* survey taken by 217 Formula One drivers saw Prost voted as the fourth greatest Formula One driver of all time, behind Senna, Schumacher, and Fangio.[[102]](#cite_note-107) Prost's teammate [Keke Rosberg](/wiki/Keke_Rosberg "Keke Rosberg") said that "He's the best I've ever known, no question about it. As an all-round race driver he's head and shoulders clear of anyone else."[[95]](#cite_note-:28-100) Formula One CEO [Bernie Ecclestone](/wiki/Bernie_Ecclestone "Bernie Ecclestone") said that Prost was the greatest driver of all time, as Prost rarely enjoyed number one driver treatment, unlike Senna or Schumacher.[[103]](#cite_note-108)[[104]](#cite_note-109) In 2023, Ecclestone said that [Max Verstappen](/wiki/Max_Verstappen "Max Verstappen") had surpassed Prost.[[105]](#cite_note-110) [Jordan](/wiki/Jordan_Grand_Prix "Jordan Grand Prix") team boss [Eddie Jordan](/wiki/Eddie_Jordan "Eddie Jordan") shared Ecclestone's opinion, appreciating that Prost "never minded who his teammate was"[[106]](#cite_note-111) (Senna being a notable exception). Formula One medical chief [Sid Watkins](/wiki/Sid_Watkins "Sid Watkins") said that Prost and Niki Lauda were the most intelligent drivers he had worked with, noting that he could recall only one dangerous auto accident involving Prost in his career.[[107]](#cite_note-112)

Various outlets have attempted to develop models that objectively measure driver skill relative to car quality. Prost generally places highly in these comparisons.

* [University of Sheffield](/wiki/University_of_Sheffield "University of Sheffield") (2016): Second all-time[[108]](#cite_note-113)
* *[The Economist](/wiki/The_Economist "The Economist")* (2020): Third all-time[[109]](#cite_note-114)
* Carteret Analytics (2020): Eighth all-time[[110]](#cite_note-115)
* F1-Analysis.com (2022): Fourth all-time; second all-time after correcting for era differences[[111]](#cite_note-116)

In the season 1 finale, she finds out that Harvey's associate (Mike Ross) has been practicing law without a degree. Rather than fire him, Harvey persuades her to retain Mike and himself so they can be well-equipped against Daniel Hardman, the other founding partner who returned after a years-long absence. After a long-waged power struggle in season 2, Jessica removes Hardman's name off the wall and merges with Edward Darby, creating Pearson Darby. She then promotes Harvey to name partner in season 3 and removes Edward Darby's name off the wall, creating Pearson Specter. In season 4, Louis Litt leverages Mike Ross's fraud into becoming a name partner. In season 6, Mike is caught and sentenced to two years in prison; however, he is able to save Jessica, Louis, and Harvey from being put in prison. In mid-season 6, Jessica chooses to leave corporate law and move to Chicago with her lover, Jeff Malone. However, prosecutor Anita Gibbs's attack on Mike forces Jessica to return and proclaim that she knew about Mike's fraud in his hearing to become a lawyer – causing her to get disbarred. She appears in season 7 on various occasions.
* [Amanda Schull](/wiki/Amanda_Schull "Amanda Schull") as [Katrina Amanda Bennett](/wiki/Katrina_Bennett "Katrina Bennett") (recurring seasons 2–7; main seasons 8–9):[[17]](#cite_note-18) A former fifth-year associate hired by Harvey and later Louis's associate; in the fallout when Louis almost leaves the firm, she goes to work for Robert Zane, Rachel's father, but returns to Specter Litt in season 6 and becomes a senior partner in season 8. By the end of the series, she is a named partner of Litt Wheeler Williams Bennett.

At age 31, Thompson was the oldest member of the 2004 U.S. Swimming and Diving team, competing in her fourth Olympics in Athens, Greece. She was the anchor member of the 400-meter freestyle relay, where she contributed to a national record of 3:36.39 and a silver medal. She earned another silver medal as a member of the 4×100-meter medley relay. During her Olympic career, Thompson won twelve medals, eight of which were relay gold; the most for any female Olympic swimmer in history.[[1]](#cite_note-sr-1)

Through her management company, TAS Rights Management, LLC, Swift has filed over 300 trademark applications in the US and holds more than 400 registrations worldwide, as of August 2025. Her filings include her name "Taylor Swift", her fanbase name "Swifties", album and tour titles, lyrics, slogans, artwork, and her cats' names.[[465]](#cite_note-465) In 2026, Swift filed to trademark her voice and appearance against [AI-generated reproductions](/wiki/Generative_AI "Generative AI"), following unauthorized [uses of her likeness in deepfake pornography](/wiki/Taylor_Swift_deepfake_pornography_controversy "Taylor Swift deepfake pornography controversy") and presidential election advertisements.[[466]](#cite_note-466)
